entities.summary:
Constantine III of Abkhazia: A key figure in the Abkhazian Kingdom of the Classical era, Constantine III played a significant role in the regional politics of the Caucasus.

Born in the 9th century, Constantine III ascended to the throne in 912 CE and ruled until his death in 923 CE. During his reign, he oversaw the expansion of the Abkhazian Kingdom, which stretched from the Black Sea to the Caucasus Mountains.

Constantine III was a prominent leader who collaborated with other regional powers, including the Kingdom of Georgia and the Byzantine Empire. He also implemented economic reforms that strengthened the Abkhazian economy and promoted trade with neighboring regions.

The legacy of Constantine III can be seen in the enduring cultural heritage of the Abkhazian people, who continue to celebrate their unique history and traditions.

This reign marked the apex of the Abkhazian Kingdom's power and influence, shaping the regional politics of the Caucasus for centuries to come.
